_readme: The shop's categories and variant options, in one place. Edit this file, run
`php .ftp-sync/publish-site.php` (add OMC_DB=live for the live store) and the store matches it.
categories  — the browse tree. `menu` decides whether a group shows in the Shop mega menu.
attributes  — the variant types. Each becomes a WooCommerce global attribute (pa_<slug>).
`type` is how the option is picked on the product page: color | button | select.
Color terms carry a swatch hex the theme and the Variation Swatches plugin read.
presets     — which variant types a product in that category normally uses, in order.
The Variation tiers tab pre-fills these, so a new product starts with the right
levels instead of a blank grid. An empty list means a one-of-a-kind piece:
no variants, just the stock count.
retire      — categories to delete. Products are never deleted, they only lose the term.
Anything not listed here is left alone.
retire_attributes — global attributes (pa_<slug>) to delete. Their terms go with them;
products keep existing and simply lose that attribute.
unpublish_products — demo products to set to draft (never deleted).
sort_skip — words meaning "not a garment", so shoes and bags are not filed as clothing types.

unpublish_products._why: Menswear and kidswear from the theme's demo import. The Men and Kids categories were retired, but the products stayed and were re-filed into womenswear categories, so the home page showed a man's shirt under Blouses and a boy's tee under Tees. Set to draft rather than deleted: nothing is lost, and re-publishing one is a click. Identified by looking at the product photographs, not by guessing from titles.

sort_skip._why: Titles that are footwear or an accessory, not a garment type. Without this, "Ethyl Low Top Sneaker" matched the Tops rule and a shoe became the Tops category tile.
